verdicts.binding_constraint: COMPLETENESS + UNRESOLVED DURABILITY, not price. Base 10y IRR +10.2% clears the 8% hurdle with 2.2pt cushion at the current price. What caps the position is three dated evidence gaps -- FY2026 full-year + TurboTax unit comparison (2026-08-25), FY2026 ARPC / paying-customer growth (FY2026 10-K, ~early Sept), and any quantified AI monetization (Investor Day 2026-09-17) -- all of which resolve within six weeks.

module_signals.finding: Primary-source base is strong: FY2025 10-K, FY26 Q3 10-Q, and three 8-Ks (FY25 Q4 / FY26 Q2 / FY26 Q3 earnings releases) all fetched directly from SEC EDGAR with full text, plus the 2026-03-16 Item 7.01 8-K verbatim. Price double-sourced at delta 0.00%. Weakness: policy status, competitive share, and every earnings-call quote rest on B-tier secondary transcripts (O6); FY2026 full-year is structurally absent (O1).

Two distinct mechanisms, not one. QuickBooks/GBS is a genuine annuity locked by plumbing (bank/card feeds and reconciliation history, 50-state payroll tax registration, embedded payments + QuickBooks Capital lending, ~1M accountant channel, audit-grade cost of migrating books) -- 9M FY26 QBO Accounting +24%, Online Ecosystem +20%, mid-market +38%. TurboTax is a different mechanism: a deliberate trade of units for price (federal units down four straight years, FY22 42.7M -> FY25 39.2M -> FY26E -2%; ARPU +11%; TurboTax Live +36% to $2.8B = 53% of TurboTax revenue). The arithmetic still works, but the moat has migrated from DISTRIBUTION to EXPERT NETWORK + BRAND, which is thinner and collides with AI directly.

GBS segment operating margin 76.7% (vs 76.8% PY) with no visible crack -- this leg alone supports the current market cap. Offsetting: Consumer segment operating margin fell 82.4% -> 80.8% (-1.6pt); TurboTax e-file share quantified DOWN ~1pt for the first time; Mailchimp (~7% of revenue per Goldman est.) is a failed $12B acquisition now declining YoY with no impairment taken; Credit Karma is a credit-cycle flow business (FY2023 already printed -9% revenue / -19% segment operating income), not a moat.

The earnings base GREW through the drawdown: TTM revenue +11.1%, TTM GAAP diluted EPS +19.9% ($13.67 -> $16.39), TTM FCF +26.7% ($6,123M -> $7,755M). Capex is 0.45% of revenue. Net cash +$0.6B at 2026-04-30. Deductions: FY2026 OCF is inflated by a ~$1.4B one-time deferred-tax release (LT DTA $1,222M -> $113M; 9M deferred taxes +$1,150M vs -$278M PY) that will not repeat; SBC is $1,549M over 9M (9.6% of revenue) and $3,341M of buybacks was needed just to take diluted shares 283 -> 279; both segment operating margins fell YoY; a 17% workforce reduction (~3,100 of ~18,200) with $300-340M of charges lands in Q4.

The real risk is narrow and specific: structural TurboTax unit loss plus a pricing ceiling. The bear mechanism is credible on cost structure (Goldman: an AI model can process a standard individual return for ~$0.12 against up to $162 paid to TurboTax) and Intuit's own disclosure already shows leakage (units down four years, share -1pt, pay-nothing customers 8M -> 7M, 'We lost on price'). NOT a franchise-death case though: the policy threat was REFUTED this cycle (IRS Direct File cancelled for the 2026 season), no AI tax product has any demonstrated e-file share, and the QuickBooks leg shows zero deterioration. Trap-shape is 'one cracking leg priced as four dead legs', not a value trap.

100% of the -60.1% drawdown is multiple compression: (1+19.9% EPS) x (1-66.8% P/E) = -60.2%, and (1+26.7% FCF) x (1-69.2% P/FCF) = -61.0%, both reconciling to the actual -60.1%. At $321.91 the base 10y IRR is +10.2% versus an 8% hurdle, with bear -5.9% and bull +19.8%. Implied expectations from the current price require only ~4-9% OE/share CAGR (i.e. ~1-6% at the company level) -- the market is pricing Intuit close to no growth for a decade. Price is NOT the binding constraint here.

drawdown_decomposition.conclusion: 100% of the drawdown is multiple compression; the earnings base grew 20-27%.

The ONLY operating line cut was TurboTax (approximately 8% -> approximately 7%). GAAP operating income guidance fell only because it absorbs the $300M restructuring charge.

segment_verdicts.size: ~25% of revenue and operating income (Goldman est.)
segment_verdicts.where_the_moat_actually_is: NOT in computing the tax (an LLM can). In: IRS Authorized e-File Provider / EFIN credentialing and the MeF transmission channel; accuracy guarantees and audit-representation liability (who pays when it is wrong); 50 separate state regimes; eight-to-nine-figure annual customer-acquisition spend.
segment_verdicts.verdict: Moat is real but THINNING, and the leak is company-admitted. Federal units down four straight years (FY22 42.7M -> FY25 39.2M, -8.2% cumulative; FY26E -2%); e-file share quantified DOWN ~1pt for the first time; pay-nothing customers 8M -> 7M; CEO: 'We lost on price'. BUT the arithmetic still works: ARPU +11%, TurboTax Live +36% to $2.8B (53% of TurboTax revenue), Live customers +38%, paying units +2%. Intuit is deliberately abandoning the low end and moving upmarket -- accounting-positive, strategically a surrender of DISTRIBUTION. HAIRCUT, NOT VETO.

segment_verdicts.where_the_moat_actually_is: The interface is trivially copyable by AI; the PLUMBING is not. Four layers: (1) direct bank/card data connections plus years of reconciliation history; (2) 50-state payroll tax registration and remittance as registered agent; (3) embedded payments (money-transmitter licensing, payment flow, QuickBooks Capital lending off that flow); (4) ~1 million accountants as a channel -- accountants do not migrate their clients' books. Migration cost is audit-grade: transaction history + reconciliations + payroll history + tax filings.
segment_verdicts.verdict: ZERO deterioration anywhere in the disclosed data. 9M FY2026 QBO Accounting +24%, Online Ecosystem +20%, GBS +17%; FY2025 ARPC +14%, paying customers +5%; mid-market (QBO Advanced + Intuit Enterprise Suite) +38%; online payment volume +30%. Only crack: paying-customer growth 6% -> 5% (growth leaning harder on price) and international only +9-10%. AI is currently Intuit's WEAPON on this leg, not its enemy. This leg alone supports the current market cap.

segment_verdicts.size: ~11% of revenue; FY2025 segment operating margin 37%
segment_verdicts.where_the_moat_actually_is: Not a software moat at all. It is credit-cycle traffic arbitrage on ~140M member credit profiles plus lender/issuer matching relationships.
segment_verdicts.verdict: NOT an AI story -- a CYCLE story. FY2026 decelerating quarter by quarter: +27% -> +23% -> +15%, with growth almost entirely from personal loans and auto insurance, the two most cyclical verticals. FY2023 already printed -9% revenue and -19% segment operating income when the credit cycle turned. Member count never disclosed. Apply a cyclical discount; do not credit it with a moat premium.

segment_verdicts.size: ~7% of revenue, ~$1.5B (Goldman est.; Intuit never discloses it)
segment_verdicts.where_the_moat_actually_is: Essentially nowhere. Marketing copy and email sequences are the single best LLM use case, and switching cost is exporting a contact list.
segment_verdicts.verdict: The ONLY leg where the AI thesis is confirmed by data rather than narrative. Evidence chain closes on primary sources: company-stated ex-Mailchimp growth gap (Q3 FY26 GBS +15% reported vs +17% ex-Mailchimp; Online Ecosystem +19% vs +22%); the 10-Q MD&A increment bridge implies Mailchimp ~-$2M in Q3 and ~-$15M over 9M; CFO admits revenue 'was down slightly' and that Intuit is 'rightsizing our investment in Mailchimp'; the return-to-double-digit-growth target slipped from 'exiting fiscal 2026' (Nov 2025) to 'some time beyond fiscal 2026' (Feb 2026 press release, A1). A $12B (2021) acquisition, still carried with NO impairment. This is realized value destruction and a negative capital-allocation data point.

policy_risk_assessed_independently.cost_cited_by_treasury: $41M to operate for tax year 2024, at least $138 per return
policy_risk_assessed_independently.legislative_successor: OBBBA Section 70607 directs Treasury to study public-private partnership replacement models -- directionally FAVOURABLE to Intuit, not adverse.
implications: The policy threat EASED across the entire drawdown window rather than worsening. Direct File was killed on 2025-11-03/05 and the stock kept falling that month -- the market was not pricing policy.

The 2026-05-21 -20.02% day had nothing to do with policy: management attributed the shortfall to price competition among DIY filers earning under $50,000 and said explicitly 'None of this has anything to do with AI.'

Therefore attributing TurboTax share loss to government encroachment is WRONG. The actual leakage is to private free/low-price competitors plus Intuit's own deliberate abandonment of the low end (pay-nothing 8M -> 7M is strategy, not theft).
Residual open risk: the Section 70607 public-private replacement is an undetermined variable, and the FTC / multistate 'free' advertising matters were NOT verified this run (O10).

runner_dissent: Attacking the optimistic side first: my base OE CAGR of 8% assumes QuickBooks keeps compounding and Consumer holds on price. Goldman's mechanism is not nonsense -- an AI model can process a standard individual return for roughly $0.12 against up to $162 paid to TurboTax. Historically, when a product's cost structure is compressed by three orders of magnitude and the remaining moat is credentialing plus brand plus ad budget, ten-year survival is not the base rate. Worse, Intuit's own response -- ceding free filers, moving upmarket -- is accounting-positive but strategically a surrender of DISTRIBUTION, and the expert-network wall is thinner than the distribution wall was. And I am grading TurboTax on a haircut rather than a veto largely because the real FY2026 unit data does not exist until 2026-08-25. If that print shows -5% instead of -2%, the base case in this card must be rewritten. Attacking the pessimistic side: the hardest set of facts in this dossier is that in a year Intuit was supposedly being destroyed by AI, it RAISED revenue guidance, RAISED non-GAAP EPS guidance, grew TTM free cash flow 26.7%, and on 2026-03-16 the founder and the entire executive leadership team terminated every outstanding 10b5-1 sell plan while accelerating buybacks against a new $8B authorization. Insiders halting sales and buying harder after a halving is one of the few non-financial signals this framework weights heavily. The cross-sectional read is sharper still: the pure tax comparable H&R Block fell only 16.1% over the identical window while the Nasdaq-100 ROSE 25.8% -- INTU underperformed the index by ~86 points. If this were truly 'AI kills tax preparation', HRB would not be nearly untouched. That spread argues what got repriced was Intuit's MULTIPLE, not Intuit's business. Why this still stops at STARTER 2%: not price (price already clears with cushion) and not the business (GBS alone supports the market cap), but three specific gaps with hard unlock dates -- FY2026 full-year and the unit comparison (2026-08-25), FY2026 ARPC and paying customers (FY2026 10-K, early September), and any quantified AI monetization (Investor Day 2026-09-17). All three land inside six weeks. On a name with -46% of downside room and +20% of bull IRR, buying the right to be in the room with 2% and deciding on 6% after those three datasets is the correct SHAPE under this framework. That is a sequencing judgement, not a courage one.
